notes: kb/Work PB1027 (landed) holds the case as an owner question it did not decide; no open note owns a fix. Not implemented: the rule's second sentence for a WRITE that precedes the file's first ADVANCING write. §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR16: "If the ADVANCING phrase is not used, automatic advancing will be provided by the implementor to act as if the user had specified AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE." SequentialConnector.WriteRecord reroutes a WRITE without the phrase to WriteAdvancingRecord (1 line, AFTER) only when SupportsVerticalPositioning holds, which is a LINAGE clause or an ADVANCING phrase already written since the OPEN; before that a record sequential file's plain WRITE is the bare record, so two of them share one line of a file the program then positions. docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4 states this as a determination and its consequence, on the ground of §2023:14.9.51.4 GR25 ("If the physical file does not support vertical positioning, the ADVANCING and END-OF-PAGE phrases are ignored"), a sentence the 1985 rule does not have (the row's change record: 2023 adds that case); the 1985 text makes only the phrase hardware dependent (§1985:C.3 item 19: "dependent upon a device capable of vertical positioning"), and a file whose ADVANCING phrases are honoured is on such a device. A file written with no ADVANCING phrase at all and no LINAGE clause is left unpositioned (no line feed between its records); this record reads that file as no "representation of a printed page" and counts only the mixed file. Implemented at 85, the rest: BindAdvancing binds the one phrase (ScreenAdvancingCount refuses a negative or non-integer integer-1 and a non-integer identifier-2, COBOL2365; VisitWriteBeforeAfter refuses the 2023 BEFORE AFTER pair, COBOL0900), EmitWrite passes it through AdvanceArg, and WriteAdvancingRecord presents before the advance for BEFORE and after it for AFTER (items e, f). Position advances n lines (item a); zero is no line feed, the next line overprinting (item c, WriteTravel and Present); a mnemonic-name advances by its feature-name's rule (item d, FeatureAdvancing: C01 as PAGE, CSP zero lines); PAGE on a LINAGE file goes to the first line of the next logical page (item g, PositionOnLogicalPage, BeginNextLogicalPage) and otherwise writes a form feed (item h, Advance). A negative identifier-2 (item b, undefined) takes the PAGE arm. Probed at --std 85 on a record sequential print file: each of these arms byte for byte, a plain WRITE after an ADVANCING write equal to AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE, and the LINAGE file of the witness line by line. The witness runs LINAGE-COUNTER through items a, c, g and the omitted phrase, and reads back a print file written BEFORE 2, BEFORE 1, AFTER 1, AFTER 3 and plain.

next.reason: 1985: "If the ADVANCING phrase is used, advancing is provided as follows:"; 2023: "If the physical file does not support vertical positioning, the ADVANCING and END-OF-PAGE phrases are ignored.". 2023 adds cases: the phrases are ignored on files without vertical positioning, and both AFTER and BEFORE may be used together. It drops the implementor-defined page repositioning sentence.
